done_when: When core.hooksPath is husky's folder, forge sync puts one line that runs Forge's pre-commit and pre-push checks (through .forge/hooks.sh) into the repo's committed .husky/pre-commit and .husky/pre-push, keeping their existing lines, and writes no shims into the folder husky rebuilds; the checks still run after npm install rebuilds that folder, in every worktree and a fresh clone; doctor reports the hooks installed in that setup; repos without husky keep today's shims; command tests cover a new husky repo and a husky repo adopted on an earlier release (including its earlier .pre-forge shims cleaned up)

findings.body: Appending the check after arbitrary existing hook code can silently disable it. An existing `.husky/pre-commit` or `.husky/pre-push` ending in `exit 0` or a successful `exec` never reaches Forge. A pre-push hook that consumes stdin reaches Forge with EOF instead: `pre_push` at `src/forge/githooks.py:128` then checks no refs and returns success, bypassing both default-branch and fix-size checks. Git supplies those refs on stdin ([hook contract](https://git-scm.com/docs/githooks#_pre_push)). The previous shim preserved and replayed input; the new tests use only echo commands, which expose neither failure. Compose the checks so existing hook control flow cannot skip them and both consumers receive the push input.
findings.title: Keep Forge checks reachable and preserve pre-push input

findings.body: Adding both user hooks to this inventory also makes them eligible for close's automatic generated-file conflict resolution. `src/forge/close.py:323` obtains that inventory, and line 329 restores every conflicting inventory file entirely from the default branch before running sync. If a Forge branch and main change the same existing command in either `.husky/pre-commit` or `.husky/pre-push`, close now silently discards the branch's hook changes and commits the default-branch version. Previously these user scripts produced an ordinary merge-conflict refusal. Exclude user hook contents from this overwrite path or preserve both sides through an explicit merge.
findings.title: Preserve user hook edits when close resolves merge conflicts

findings.body: Two claimed proof details are not protected by their named tests. In `test_committed_husky_checks_survive_install_in_worktrees_and_fresh_clone`, this assertion counts `forge hook` but never verifies `.forge/hooks.sh` is used; replacing the emitted command with a direct Forge invocation would still pass because Forge is already on the fixture's PATH. In `tests/test_fix_upgrade_untracked_hooks.py::test_1_untracked_hook_files_never_block_an_upgrade_but_a_stale_tracked_file_does`, the test command creates `.husky/_/h` in the working checkout only after the synced-file check. That check runs sync in a separate worktree (`src/forge/close.py:360`) and inspects it at line 364; the new sync creates no runtime files there. Removing the runtime exclusion at `src/forge/close.py:380` would therefore leave this proof passing. Add command-level assertions that detect bypassing the launcher and actually present untracked runtime files to the status check.
findings.title: Not done: launcher routing and generated-runtime exclusion proofs

why: In client repos that use husky, every npm install rebuilds husky's hooks folder (core.hooksPath .husky/_) and wipes Forge's pre-commit and pre-push shims, so doctor reports the git hooks missing in every worktree after install (reported by a client session on v1.2.7). Owner decision 2026-10-08: add Forge to husky's own committed hooks
